goals: Mechanistic: quantify the sensitivity/strength of ELM sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) to soil texture across the basin's agricultural soils under fixed forcing
Validation: check simulated sub-surface hydrology against in-domain observations
key_processes: soil water partitioning (drainage vs surface runoff vs ET)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly resolves soil-texture control on water partitioning; stratifying columns by real soil texture under uniform forcing isolates the texture effect the question asks about.

answerable: Strength/direction of soil-texture control on sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) via a texture-stratified column set under uniform forcing
Relative partitioning shifts (drainage vs runoff vs ET) across texture classes

not_answerable.aspect: Observational validation of sub-surface drainage magnitude in this tile-drained landscape
not_answerable.why: The dominant real drainage pathway is artificial tile drains, and tile-drain flow data are missing in-domain; ELM does not explicitly represent tile drainage
not_answerable.needs: tile-drain flow observation ingest + ELM tile-drainage representation

not_answerable.why: Forcing is uniform (no elevation downscaling); a texture-stratified set cannot attribute variation to elevation

sampling_strategy.n_justification: One driver with ~5 texture classes spanning coarse to fine; 2 replicates per class expose within-class spread from secondary soil properties while keeping N minimal and defensible. Denser sampling adds no new mechanism for a single-driver question.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate exploratory columns across the agricultural footprint to span the full soil-texture gradient (coarse well-drained to fine poorly-drained); the downstream expander samples the real gridded soil raster to assign class membership.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 per texture class to capture within-class variability in hydraulic properties, not to resolve a second driver.

sampling_plan.reason: High-Ksat end-member: expected maximum drainage fraction, anchors the texture-sensitivity curve at the coarse end.
Moderately coarse soils bridging coarse and medium textures to resolve the drainage-response gradient.
Medium-texture central case representative of much of the agricultural landscape.
Fine, poorly drained soils where drainage should drop and runoff/retention rise.
Low-Ksat end-member: expected minimum drainage, anchors the fine end of the sensitivity curve.

validation_design.comparison: aggregated/co-located where wells fall near columns — treated as a weak indirect check because ELM lacks explicit tile drainage and wells are sparse
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well density; likely few

validation_design.comparison: none — no in-domain observations; flagged as a validation gap

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline uniform forcing (1980-2018 climatology), native per-column soil texture from raster

requires_capabilities.why: Primary drainage pathway in this agricultural basin is tiles; no data source is wired in
Standard ELM QDRAI does not represent engineered tile drains
requires_capabilities.blocks: physically faithful drainage magnitudes for tiled fields

requires_capabilities.why: Needed to attribute any drainage variation to elevation/climate
Assign real texture class to each stratified column

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well observation ingest + co-location resolver
requires_capabilities.why: Pin any validation columns to sparse wells and match depths
Soil moisture and drainage fluxes require equilibration before analysis

assumptions: Uniform forcing applied to all columns; texture is the only varied driver.
Soil-texture classes and their spatial extent come from a gridded soil raster sampled downstream; the five classes listed are placeholders to be confirmed against the actual raster.
Water table from sparse USGS wells is only a weak indirect proxy for drainage in a tiled landscape.
Analysis window drawn from 1980-2018; representative multi-year period chosen downstream.
open_questions: Which soil-texture classes actually dominate the basin per the raster, and are five strata sufficient?
How many USGS wells fall usefully near candidate columns, and over what period?
Is any tile-drain flow record obtainable (even at an analog site) to anchor drainage magnitudes?
Should drainage sensitivity be reported per-class absolute QDRAI or as fractional partitioning shifts?
